edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 45,000,000 for the Shares at Closing, subject to customary post-signing and/or closing adjustments, including as applicable debt, cash, working capital, and leakage adjustments, to be determined in accordance with a mutually agreed closing statement and the adjustment methodology set forth in this Agreement.

2. Closing. Closing shall occur on a date mutually agreed by the parties, but in any event no later than 45 days after signing (the "Outside Date"), subject to the satisfaction or waiver of customary closing conditions, including completion of the parties' agreed diligence to the Buyer’s reasonable satisfaction, the accuracy of the representations and warranties at Closing subject to applicable materiality qualifiers, and delivery of the agreed closing deliverables.

3. Representations. The Seller represents, subject to customary qualifiers and limitations, that: (a) it has good title to the Shares, free and clear of all encumbrances (other than any permitted encumbrances expressly disclosed in writing); (b) it has the requisite authority and power to enter into and perform this Agreement; (c) the Shares are duly authorized, validly issued, fully paid and non-assessable; (d) the business has been conducted in compliance in all material respects with applicable law; (e) there are no undisclosed liabilities of a type that would be required to be reflected in accordance with GAAP (other than those arising in the ordinary course or otherwise disclosed); (f) there is no material litigation pending or, to the Seller’s knowledge, threatened; (g) all material taxes have been properly reported and paid, subject to reserves and ordinary-course exceptions; (h) employee matters have been managed in material compliance with applicable law; and (i) the material contracts identified by the parties are in full force and effect, subject to customary exceptions.

4. Confidentiality. The terms of this Agreement are confidential, except that a party may disclose such terms (i) as required by applicable law, regulation, court order, or any governmental authority; (ii) to its affiliates and its and their respective directors, officers, employees, advisers, auditors, insurers, and potential financing sources, in each case who are subject to confidentiality obligations no less protective than those herein or are otherwise bound by professional or legal duties of confidentiality; and (iii) in connection with any permitted enforcement of rights under this Agreement, provided that, to the extent legally permissible, the disclosing party gives prompt prior notice to the other party and uses commercially reasonable efforts to minimize the scope of any disclosure.

5. Indemnification. Subject to the limitations in this Agreement, the Seller shall indemnify the Buyer for losses arising from breaches of the Seller's representations, warranties, and covenants. Any claims for breach of representations and warranties shall survive for 12 months after Closing, except that fundamental representations, tax matters, fraud, and covenants expressly intended to survive shall survive for the applicable statute of limitations or such other period as expressly stated. The Seller's aggregate liability shall be capped at 10% of the Purchase Price, provided that claims for fraud shall not be subject to such cap. The Buyer shall not be entitled to recover unless and until losses exceed a basket equal to 1% of the Purchase Price, at which point recovery shall be limited to losses in excess of the basket.

6. Termination Right. If Closing has not occurred by the Outside Date due primarily to Seller-related matters, the Buyer may terminate this Agreement upon written notice, without prejudice to any rights it may have arising from the Seller's prior breach, subject to the limitations and procedures set forth in this Agreement.

receiver.requested_changes:
1. Purchase Price: Reduce the headline price to USD 42,500,000, or at minimum retain USD 45,000,000 only if there is no leakage and the buyer receives a more favorable escrow/indemnity package. Clarify that all leakage is fully compensated on a dollar-for-dollar basis and that the purchase price adjustment mechanics are set out in a buyer-favorable closing statement process.
2. Closing: Extend the Outside Date to 60–75 days after signing. Remove the open-ended “mutually agreed” closing date concept and require Closing to occur on a fixed date after conditions are satisfied. Limit closing conditions to objective items within the seller’s control, and delete the buyer-satisfaction diligence standard. Add a buyer walk-right if any material adverse change occurs.
3. Representations: Strengthen the seller reps and reduce qualifiers. Add standard reps on organization, capitalization, no broker fees, title, subsidiaries, no undisclosed indebtedness, no material adverse change, compliance, permits, IP, litigation, labor, data/privacy, sanctions/anti-corruption, and solvency. Tighten the “knowledge,” “material,” and “ordinary course” qualifiers, and require disclosure schedules. For the fundamental reps, make them unqualified and bring them to bring-down at closing.
4. Confidentiality: Narrow the carve-outs. Any disclosure to affiliates, financing sources, or advisers should be only on a need-to-know basis and subject to written confidentiality obligations at least as protective as this Agreement. For any legally compelled disclosure, require prior notice unless prohibited by law and allow the Buyer to seek protective relief.
5. Indemnification: Increase seller liability and lengthen survival. General reps should survive 18–24 months; fundamental reps, tax, fraud, title, and authority should survive through the applicable statute or a longer negotiated period. Raise the cap on general claims to at least 20%–30% of the Purchase Price, or full recovery for specified breaches. Replace the tipping basket with a deductible basket, or remove the basket entirely for certain core reps. Carve out fraud, title, authority, capitalization, taxes, and leakage from all limitations. Add an express right of setoff/escrow holdback.
6. Termination: Buyer’s termination right should not be limited to delay “due primarily to Seller-related matters.” The Buyer should have a unilateral right to terminate if Closing has not occurred by the Outside Date for any reason other than Buyer breach, plus an express right to terminate for any material seller breach before Closing.
7. Additional items: Include a comprehensive disclosure schedule requirement, bring in escrow/holdback mechanics for indemnity, and confirm no debt assumption except as expressly stated. Please circulate a clean version with these points reflected.
